q: Our landlord put solar on the roof of our rented factory. Who claims it?
title: Solar on a rented roof: who claims
short: Whoever uses the power can count it, but only once. If you consume the solar units, your Scope 2 falls by that amount. If the landlord sells them to you under a contract, keep the contract and meter readings. The landlord cannot also claim units you used.

ul: Landlord's panels feed your meter: your Scope 2 drops.
Landlord sells solar units to you: market-based claim with the contract.
Landlord exports to the grid: you see no change.

p: A clause stating who claims the solar attributes avoids double counting later.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
